benchmarkScope: isolated calculation pipeline, not an authenticated React page
limitations: View-only main reference reuses generated items but does not reproduce every React useMemo cache; worker currently recomputes and returns the full result.
No application DOM rendering, authenticated flow, real account, real phone, memory-pressure or battery test.
CPU throttling is measured separately for main and worker; it must not be assumed equivalent to a real phone.
Five timing repetitions per variant in one desktop Chrome. Full output equality was checked in 27 dedicated cases, not by a new full hash in all 240 timing trials.
Rapid bursts of filter changes were not benchmarked. Aborting the older Promise ignores its response but does not interrupt running or already queued worker computation.
Long-task causes have not been profiled with a trace; the remaining 71 ms task cannot be attributed solely to structured clone.

decision: Do not deploy the naive full-input/full-result worker. Prototype needs lower transfer overhead and reuse of calculations; verify in actual application before release.
throttlingInterpretation: Calibration confirms CDP 4x throttles main thread but not the worker comparably. Use native 1x results for the main-versus-worker comparison; 4x is only a diagnostic of main-thread pressure, not a real-phone speedup.
metricInterpretation: timerDelayMs probes initial task blocking only; return-message deserialization can block later. Long-task counts and rAF gaps must also be considered. rAF timing is not INP, and no application rendering was measured.
serializationInterpretation: inputJsonBytes/resultJsonBytes measure JSON representation size only. The benchmark uses structured clone, which preserves Date and shared references; these values are not transferred network or structured-clone byte counts.

independentReview.recommendation: Do not deploy this naive prototype.
